title: Short-run handback lattice — two-week rotation (Apr 2026)
content:
Purpose: lightweight two-week rotation grid to coordinate ad-hoc handbacks, short-run surge coverage, and cross-functional contacts. Intended to be copied into daily standup notes and referenced in #ops-handback when making ad-hoc swaps.

How to use: (1) maintain owner rows for each window; (2) update Status column live; (3) add quick notes for blocking items and link a ticket when available. This is intentionally compact — keep action items short.

Columns (spreadsheet):
- Window (UTC): two-week windows, primary timezone used for handback start.
- Owner (name + role): person responsible for that window.
- Primary contact (email / slack): quickest route for an ask.
- Coverage focus: what to prioritize during the window (e.g., routing faults, latency spikes, fallbacks).
- Escalation path: who to page if owner is unavailable.
- Status: green / amber / red + short rationale.
- Last update (ISO): date/time of last change.
- Linked ticket(s): jira / PRs for current work.
- Quick notes / ToDo: 1-2 line entry; include "(blocking)" marker where appropriate.

Current grid (sample rows):
1) Window: 2026-04-20T00:00Z — 2026-05-04T00:00Z
   Owner: Aisha Coleman (Product Ops)
   Primary contact: aisha@redwood.com / slack @aisha
   Coverage focus: routing fallback coverage across us-west / eu-central, keep canary routes warm
   Escalation path: Jun Park -> @oncall-sre -> Marcus Reid (lead)
   Status: amber — observing 2x latent tail on reroute path; mitigation in progress
   Last update: 2026-04-22T09:12Z
   Linked ticket(s): OPS-3842 (routing fallback investigation)
   Quick notes: temp throttle policy applied 04-21; need capacity bump request to infra (see linked PR)

2) Window: 2026-04-20T08:00Z — 2026-05-04T08:00Z (APAC overlap)
   Owner: Jun Park (Solutions Eng)
   Primary contact: jun@redwood.com / slack @junp
   Coverage focus: private-deploy onboarding smoke tests (apac cluster), on-call for customer pilot
   Escalation path: Lena Ortiz -> eng-dedicated -> support-lead
   Status: green — pilot tests passing, one flaky e2e next week
   Last update: 2026-04-21T18:45Z
   Linked ticket(s): https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/PD-211 (pilot e2e flaky)
   Quick notes: coordinate with customer success for weekend run, capture logs to S3 (temp bucket c-ops-handback)

3) Window: 2026-04-20T16:00Z — 2026-05-04T16:00Z (EU prime)
   Owner: Lena Ortiz (Eng PM)
   Primary contact: lena@redwood.com / slack @lena_o
   Coverage focus: observability spikes — embedding batch jobs causing transient CPU climb
   Escalation path: Marcus Reid -> eng-observability -> infra-oncall
   Status: amber — batch scheduling offset change queued
   Last update: 2026-04-22T07:03Z
   Linked ticket(s): https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/OBS-1290
   Quick notes: shift batch window by 90m (proposal in PR #72); monitor token-cost trend for embeddings

4) Window: floating reserve (ad-hoc)
   Owner: Marcus Reid (SRE) — reserve holder for emergency coverage
   Primary contact: marcus@redwood.com / slack @mreid
   Coverage focus: takeover for multi-region incidents, capacity reclamation
   Escalation path: oncall-manager -> exec-ops
   Status: green
   Last update: 2026-04-19T11:00Z
   Linked ticket(s): OPS-3788 (capacity reclamation playbook)
   Quick notes: reserve should take ownership if more than 2 windows show amber at once

Open action items (short):
- A: Infra capacity bump request for us-west canary (owner: Aisha) — create capacity request form and link to PR by EOD 2026-04-22.
- B: E2E flaky test triage for private-deploy pilot (owner: Jun) — attach failing trace and set repro steps in PD-211.
- C: Batch offset change monitoring window (owner: Lena) — post metrics dashboard link in #observability and tag ops rotation for first 72 hours.
- D: Update handback runbook with weekend escalation matrix (owner: Marcus) — add phone numbers and external SRE on-call lists.

Notes to self / rough thoughts:
- Keep this sheet deliberately short — if a window accumulates >3 linked tickets, escalate to longer-term rota and create a proper on-call calendar entry.
- If multiple pilots hit same time-window, mark "collision" in Notes and request reserve takeover.
- Prefer Slack for realtime pings; use email only for asynchronous handover notes.
- For any cross-region capacity changes, include cost estimate in the ticket before approval.

Quick references / copy-paste snippets for standup: 
- "Handback window check: Aisha (US) amber — routing fallback under investigation (OPS-3842). Jun (APAC) green. Lena (EU) amber — batch offset queued. Marcus reserve green."
- "Escalation: Aisha -> Jun -> Marcus -> oncall-manager"

Unresolved questions / follow-ups:
- Q1: Who can approve an immediate burst capacity request outside of scheduled commits? (expected answer: infra-ops lead or finance designee; need to add nominal $ cap in runbook)
- Q2: Should reserve holder automatically assume ownership after 6 hours of amber across >=2 windows? (proposal: yes; add rule and notify stakeholders)

Version history (short):
- 2026-04-19 created initial two-week lattice and assigned owners (Aisha).
- 2026-04-21 updated with Jun pilot status and PR #72 pointer.
- 2026-04-22 adjusted Aisha notes after telemetry review; flagged amber.

Slack refs: #ops-handback, #prod-ops, #observability
Jira refs: OPS-3842, OBS-1290, PD-211
Confluence: Two-Week Handback Guidelines (linked above)

End — keep this short and edit live during rotation.

(Notes: intended to be copied into a Google Sheet with these columns and used as daily reference; keep owners aligned and avoid duplicate rows — when a swap occurs, append a new row with the swap timestamp rather than editing historic rows.)
